about: Capture-time provenance for docs/screens/*.png (#335). One row per shot, written by the session that took the pixels: sha256/canvas are properties of the bytes, origin/install/url/seed/level/layout/sampleRate/build are properties of the instrument and cannot be recovered from the PNG afterwards. `node tools/recap.js check` verifies each row against the file it addresses and against every other row of the same (seed, level, sampleRate); the vocabulary, the route verdicts and the audio-draw rule live in tools/recap.js, not here.

The frames came back with no world pixel moved: three of the eight are byte-identical to the committed bytes and the other five differ only inside the columns the held rig occupies (0.03% to 0.39% of the frame, every mean within 0.01 luma), which is the load-to-load disagreement #611 already names, not a surface being fetched differently. The blob that moved is js/20_level.js, and what moved in it is a jump predicate (#893): a still frame cannot show it because the feet are on the ground.

shots.note: Re-taken off the deployed page for #931. The page the camera looked at was proved blob by blob before the shutter: index.html and the eleven scripts that page loads - twelve blobs - sha256-match git show ae0dd1d:<file> twelve for twelve. Build 709c934, which is what this tree ships and what the deploy serves today, differs from that build in exactly ONE shipped blob (js/20_level.js 387e394bbb23 -> af2f4dd208bf, the authored storey of #421), and recap arbiter painted the seats these rows were shot in from both trees and all three came back BYTE-IDENTICAL - so these eight rows are a re-KEY onto 709c934 and no second shutter is owed (#910: the hash says maybe, the pixels decide). Against the frame each row replaces (19d5cd2, mean 60.5823): 1,687 px / 0.15% clear the kept-pixel rule sum|dRGB| > 18, 430 / 823 / 434 top/middle/bottom, rows 104 to 762 and columns 309 to 1184, +7.06 lumas each, 60.60 mean against 60.58. Band means 60.3 / 64.0 / 57.6. What moved: 430 kept pixels sit on the view line in the top third where the posed grunt stands, at +7.06 each: the far edge he is silhouetted against is the surface that changed (#941). The grunt coverage came back at 255 raster px on a seat needing no turn, so the #922 character ramp is inside both frames. Route: one page load and one boot per pose (js/90_dev.js refuses a second DEV.boot() in a load), the camera on the seat the same deal puts it on and read back off the load that drew it, DEV.freeze(true), DEV.set("grain",0), DEV.clear() before the shutter, the display pinned to 1440x763 by livecap --vp, toDataURL handed back RGBA and the frame re-encoded to colour type 2 through tools/png_rgb.js. The two signatures these poses carry came back unchanged - ARCHIVE 4083630493, ABATOIR 2343219222 - so every figure below is a statement about paint and none about the dice. THE STACK is no longer in that list: #421 authors a storey into its plan and #917 leaves that authored deck standing above the hall's own ceiling plane, so the shipped page reads 3132488476 at the seat its frame is shot in and that one row was re-shot rather than carried (#958). The audio term is carried rather than read: headless loads expose no output device, so SND.init never sets SND.ac (#404); that term sets how many draws precede generation, so had it moved the signatures would have moved with it, and they did not.
